failures.name: Front-end collision damage
cause_chain: Impact crushes the bumper and crash structure
Radiator, lights and sensors behind it can be damaged
Leaks, warnings or unsafe structure follow
failures.test: Look behind the bumper for a cracked radiator or fluid drips.
failures.expected: Bent parts, cracked radiator or fresh fluid under the front.
fix: Do not drive if fluids leak or warnings show.
Photograph the damage for insurance.
STOP: structural and airbag-area repairs need a certified body shop.
failures.safety: For EVs and hybrids, crash damage can affect the high-voltage system. Keep clear and call the dealer.

failures.name: Tire puncture / low pressure
cause_chain: A nail or valve leak lets air escape
failures.test: Check all four tire pressures with a gauge.
failures.expected: One tire well below the door-sticker pressure.
fix: Park safely and turn on hazard lights.
Inflate to the pressure on the door sticker.
Spray soapy water to find the leak.
Fit the spare or get the puncture repaired.
failures.safety: Never drive far on a flat tire.

failures.name: Tire tread worn / uneven wear
cause_chain: Tires age or alignment is off
failures.test: Insert a coin into the tread grooves.
failures.expected: Tread below 1.6 mm or wear only on one edge.
fix: Replace tires with worn tread.
Get a wheel alignment if wear is uneven.
Rotate tires every 10,000 km.

failures.name: Tire sidewall bulge (internal damage)
cause_chain: A pothole or kerb impact breaks internal cords
failures.test: Look along the sidewall in good light.
fix: Do not drive at speed.
Fit the spare.
Replace the tire. Sidewall damage cannot be repaired.

failures.name: 12V battery weak or failing
cause_chain: Heat ages the 12V battery (common in the UAE)
failures.test: Measure battery voltage with the engine off.
failures.expected: Below 12.4 V at rest, or drops below 10 V while cranking.
fix: Turn everything off.
Jump-start or use a booster pack.
Test the battery at a service centre.
Replace if it fails the load test.
failures.safety: Protect eyes; batteries can vent gas.

failures.name: Corroded or loose battery terminals
cause_chain: Acid vapour forms crust on terminals
failures.test: Wiggle each terminal clamp by hand (engine off).
failures.expected: Crust visible or a clamp moves.
fix: Turn off the car and remove the key.
Disconnect negative first, then positive.
Clean with baking soda and water and a brush.
Reconnect positive first, then negative, and tighten.

failures.name: Alternator not charging
cause_chain: Battery is not recharged while driving
Warning light, then the car dies
failures.test: Measure battery voltage with the engine running.
fix: Avoid long drives.
Check the drive belt is intact.
Have the alternator tested and replaced at a workshop.

failures.name: Coolant leak (radiator or hose)
cause_chain: Engine runs hot and can overheat
failures.test: With the engine COLD, check the coolant reservoir level.
failures.expected: Level below MIN and drips under the radiator.
fix: Stop driving if the gauge is high.
Let the engine cool fully.
Top up with the correct coolant.
Find and replace the leaking hose or radiator.
failures.safety: Never open the radiator cap when hot: scalding risk.

failures.name: Head gasket failure
cause_chain: Gasket fails and coolant enters cylinders
failures.test: Check the oil cap for milky residue.
fix: Do not drive.
STOP: needs workshop diagnosis (compression / block test).

failures.name: Engine oil leak
cause_chain: A gasket or seal hardens and leaks
Oil drips onto hot parts or the ground
failures.test: Check the dipstick and look under the engine.
failures.expected: Oil level low and wet, dark residue on the engine.
fix: Top up oil to the correct level.
Clean the area and recheck after a short drive.
Replace the leaking gasket or seal at a workshop.
failures.safety: Oil on hot exhaust is a fire risk.

failures.name: Engine burning oil (worn rings/valve seals)
cause_chain: Piston rings or valve seals wear
failures.test: Check how much oil is used between changes.
failures.expected: More than about 1 litre per 1,000 km.
fix: Monitor oil level weekly.
STOP: engine internals need workshop repair.

failures.name: Engine misfire (plugs/coils)
cause_chain: A spark plug or ignition coil fails
failures.test: Read the OBD-II code with a scanner.
fix: Read the code to find the cylinder.
Swap that coil with a neighbour to confirm.
Replace the faulty plug or coil.
failures.safety: A flashing check-engine light means stop soon: catalyst damage risk.

failures.name: Brake pads worn
cause_chain: Wear indicator or metal touches the disc
Squeal, then grinding and weaker braking
failures.test: Look through the wheel at the pad thickness.
failures.expected: Less than 3 mm of pad left.
fix: Avoid hard braking.
Replace pads on both sides of the axle.
Measure discs and replace if scored.
failures.safety: Brakes are safety-critical. Use a qualified mechanic.

failures.name: Brake fluid low / brake system leak
cause_chain: Fluid leaks or pads wear down
Brake warning light and soft pedal
failures.test: Check the brake fluid reservoir level.
fix: Do not drive if the pedal feels soft.
STOP: brake leaks need a mechanic immediately.

failures.name: Wheel alignment / suspension issue
cause_chain: A pothole or worn part shifts alignment
Car pulls and tires wear unevenly
failures.test: Drive straight on a flat road and briefly relax your grip.
failures.expected: The car drifts to one side.
fix: Check tire pressures first.
Get a wheel alignment.
Inspect suspension joints and bushings.

failures.name: EV high-voltage battery degraded
cause_chain: Heat and fast charging age the cells
failures.test: Read the battery state-of-health in the car app or with an OBD tool.
fix: Avoid frequent 100% charges and fast charging in heat.
Park in shade.
Check battery warranty with the dealer.

failures.name: EV high-voltage system fault
cause_chain: A cell, contactor or cooling fault is detected
The car limits power or shuts down
fix: Stop safely and switch off.
Keep everyone out of the car if there is smoke or smell.
STOP: call the dealer's EV service. Do not touch orange cables.
failures.safety: High voltage: deadly. Only certified EV technicians.
